subject: Clarify: KV cache re-use & minimums for microburst-heavy workloads
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@olivehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.p@olivehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -0400
Subject: KV cache reuse & minimums question

Hi Irene,

Quick question from procurement as we finalize the SOW: our traffic pattern is a lot of very short, latency-sensitive microbursts that share a very small set of prefixes (so the KV cache gets a lot of reuse). We want to understand how that affects the monthly minimums and rounding rules. In particular: if many calls reuse the KV cache and so generate fewer tokens overall, do you still apply the per-call/session minimums (we're talking microcalls of ~50 tokens each, about 10K calls/day) or does prefix/KV reuse cause a different aggregation that could reduce minimums?

We have a tight budget and any predictable crediting/concession would be helpful. Can you point us to the exact calculation or example invoice line that would apply?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Senior Procurement Manager
OliveHealth
jordan.ellis@olivehealth.com
(512) 555-0142

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KV cache reuse & minimums question

Jordan — thanks for the clear description. Short answer: KV/prefix reuse reduces token consumption but does not automatically bypass minimums tied to the billing "atomic unit" (our per-call quantum and any active-session floor) unless you qualify for the prefix-reuse credit pilot.

High-level notes so you have something to share with your finance folks:
- Token-level charges are computed after KV cache reuse (so you pay for net tokens emitted).
- We maintain a per-request minimum (e.g., 20-token quantum) for metering granularity and a session/minimum that applies to continuous-chat sessions (your microbursts are per-call).
- We do offer a prefix-reuse offset credit for customers whose traffic is dominated by repeated short calls against the same KV set — it's a negotiated concession and must be scoped in the SOW (pilot-only by default).

I'm looping in Kim (technical billing) and Sergio (GTMS / discounts) to provide an example calc and propose a short pilot amendment.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KV cache reuse & minimums question — example calc and proposal

Jordan — attaching a worked example (kv_reuse_billing_calc.xlsx) and a simple diagram (context-heartbeat-diagram.png). TL;DR and math below.

Quoted from your note: "microbursts of ~50 tokens each, about 10K calls/day, high prefix reuse"

Assumptions used in calc:
- Per-token price: $0.00012
- Per-call quantum floor: 20 tokens (metered to 20-token increments)
- Daily microbursts: 10,000 calls 
- Average emitted tokens w/o KV reuse: 50
- Effective emitted tokens with KV reuse: 18 (we observed similar telemetry from a pilot customer where prefix KV trimmed ~32 tokens per call)

Scenario A — no prefix credit (standard billing):
- Metered per-call quantum means each call metered at 20 tokens (since 18 tokens rounds up to 20) => 10,000 * 20 = 200,000 billed tokens/day
- Cost/day = 200,000 * $0.00012 = $24.00

Scenario B — with prefix-reuse offset credit (pilot concession we suggested):
- We apply a prefix-reuse offset that reduces the effective billed tokens per call by the observed KV benefit before quantum rounding. So 18 tokens stays 18 and then is rounded to the quantum (still 20). However, for customers with sustained reuse we offer a small per-call credit that effectively reduces the quantum floor to 15 tokens for the pilot period (this is the negotiated concession). => 10,000 * 15 = 150,000 billed tokens/day
- Cost/day = 150,000 * $0.00012 = $18.00

Net impact (pilot concession): ~25% cost reduction in this example. The concession is structured as: 3-month pilot, measured traffic (>60% prefix reuse), monthly reconciliation with usage report, and one-time audit checklist. If the traffic pattern changes we revert to standard metering.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Irene / Sergio to approve pilot terms (duration / success metrics / audit)
2) Jordan / OliveHealth to sign the proposed amendment (I prepared proposed-pilot-amendment.docx)
3) Technical onboarding: we add a lightweight telemetry flag to validate prefix reuse >= 60% for the pilot.

If you want, I can also produce a simulated invoice for June (sample invoice line items) so procurement can see the exact line mapping.

—Kim
